title: Process-Variation-Aware Design Optimization for Wavelength-Routed Optical Networks-on-Chip
problem: Wavelength-routed optical NoCs use microring resonators (MRRs) for collision-free communication, but manufacturing process variation shifts MRR transmission spectra, reducing signal power and increasing crosstalk.
motivation: Optical NoCs promise low-latency communication but are sensitive to process variation; designs ignoring this degradation suffer reduced performance and reliability.
method: Methodology constructs analytical models of expected signal transmission power under MRR process variation. Optimization jointly tunes MRR radii and signal wavelengths to maximize expected signal power despite process variation. Joint tuning exploits coupled effects between geometry and wavelength selection.
key_novelty: First process-variation-aware design optimization for wavelength-routed optical NoCs, analytically modeling MRR variation and jointly optimizing radii and wavelengths.
contributions: Analytical models of expected signal power under MRR process variation
Joint optimization of MRR radii and signal wavelengths for robustness
Methodology for worst-case expected signal transmission power improvement
7.51 dB improvement in worst-case signal transmission power vs. variation-unaware designs
primary_theme: Variation-aware optical NoC design via joint MRR and wavelength optimization
